seltz.title: Manichithrathazhu
seltz.snippet:
Manichithrathazhu is a 1993 Indian Malayalam-language supernatural thriller film starring Shobana, Mohanlal, and Suresh Gopi in lead roles. The movie was directed by Fazil and produced by Appachan. The film depicts the story of a woman named Ganga, who is believed to be possessed by a spirit called Nagavalli. The movie is still considered one of the best horror films that Malayalam cinema has ever produced.

The story revolves around a joint family who moves into a century-old mansion in Kerala. They plan to convert the mansion into a homestay for tourists. The family members soon realize that the mansion has a mysterious past and the spirit of Nagavalli still haunts the premises. As they begin to sense an eerie feeling around the house, they seek the help of a psychiatrist called Dr. Sunny. Dr. Sunny was a friend to the family and he along with his wife, Annie, came to investigate the claims of the haunting.

Dr. Sunny suspects that Ganga is suffering from a multiple personality disorder and tries to treat her by delving deeper into her psyche. Dr. Sunny's wife Annie, who is hesitant at first due to the supernatural element, gets intrigued by the case and assists her husband in treating Ganga.

As the plot thickens, the family members start experiencing strange occurrences around the house. They hear noises, see apparitions, and find objects moving on their own. The story takes a thrilling turn as Ganga's personalities start to reveal themselves as that of Nagavalli, the spirit that the family was warned about.

The film's screenplay is well crafted as it blends elements of horror, comedy, and suspense. The dialogues, music, and cinematography all add to the tension of the plot. The film's music was composed by M. G. Radhakrishnan and the songs \"Oru Murai Vanthu Parthaya\" and \"Manichithrathazhu\" still enjoy a massive following in South India.

The movie is famous for its exemplary performances by the lead actors.

The lyrics in Malayalam is written by Bichu Thirumala and Madhu Muttam and lyrics in Tamil are written by Vaali. Manichitrathazhu was released on 25 December 1993, and performed well at the box office, becoming the highest-grossing Malayalam film at the time.
The film also won three Kerala state awards -- Best Film with Popular Appeal and Aesthetic Value (1994), Best Actress and Best Make-up Artist (PN Mani). The film thematically followed Swapnadanam's theme which was unusual and not common in Indian cinema at the time. The film completed 300 days of run in many theatres. Manichitrathazhu was remade in four languages – in Kannada as Apthamitra (2004) (with some plot changes) which in turn was remade in Tamil as Chandramukhi (2005), in Bengali as Rajmohol (2005) and in Hindi as Bhool Bhulaiyaa (2007)– all being commercially successful.
